# 45 Things to Make and Sell Online for Profit in 2025

By   Roland Dacillo   / Uncategorized

Starting an online business is a great way to achieve financial independence. If you want control over your work schedule and to run your own business, why not make and sell DIY crafts online?

Handmade gifts are charming and meaningful. Despite the prevalence of mass-produced items, there’s a growing trend towards DIY and personalized handmade crafts. In fact, the global art and craft market size is already at $50 billion in 2024.

The digital world is brimming with possibilities, and now is the perfect time to explore handmade and customized products. [...] , art and collectibles (21%), jewelry (15%), and clothing (11%).

The platform has over 1.4 million sellers and 19.8 million buyers, emphasizing the significant market for handmade goods. Etsy’s success is attributed to its focus on handmade and vintage items, charging sellers a listing fee and commission while offering advertising services to boost product reach.

Aside from these platforms, using high-quality product photography and engaging in social media marketing best practices can help boost your DIY business online.

### Comfort and Coziness

In the home decor market, there’s a strong trend toward cozy and inviting spaces. Products that exude warmth, such as handmade blankets, pillows, and other textiles, are in demand.

### Biophilic and Nature-Inspired Design [...] #### 19. Handcrafted Bookmarks

Themes of your handcrafted bookmarks can range from literary quotes and book characters to seasonal designs and inspirational messages. Cater to book lovers by offering a variety of designs that match different genres and tastes.

Use platforms like Goodreads, book clubs, and literary blogs to market your bookmarks. It’s also best to collaborate with authors or bookstores to reach a dedicated audience.

### Kids and Pet Products

Parents and pet owners always seek unique, high-quality items for their loved ones, so kids and pet products are ideal for a DIY online store. Personalization increases their appeal, as customized products can meet specific preferences.

#### 20. Custom Plush Toys

The global furniture market is evolving alongside changing lifestyles, expanding housing infrastructure, and rising consumer expectations for comfort, functionality, and design. Furniture Market Valued at USD 786.1 billion in 2025, the market is projected to reach USD 831.6 billion in 2026 and USD 1,334.1 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 7.0% from 2026 to 2033. Demand is increasingly influenced by residential construction, commercial development, home improvement spending, and consumer interest in space-efficient, customizable, and multifunctional furniture. At the same time, digital retail channels, sustainable materials, and technology-enabled furnishings are changing how consumers discover and purchase products.

Three Forces Reshaping the Furniture Market [...] Sustainability presents another opportunity, particularly through responsibly sourced materials, recycled inputs, durability, repairability, and product longevity. Smart furniture, including LED bedside tables and furnishings with charging functionality, represents an additional intersection between traditional home products and technology.

Conclusion

The furniture market is projected to reach USD 1,334.1 billion by 2033, supported by housing development, consumer spending on interiors, and demand across residential and commercial applications. Bedroom furniture, wood products, and residential furnishings remain central to the market, while storage solutions, plastic furniture, smart features, and commercial projects create additional opportunities. results.title: Geek Chic Shark Tank Update – Shark Tank Season 4
results.content:
## About Geek Chic

| Category | Details |
 --- |
| Business Name | Geek Chic |
| Founders | Robert Gifford |
| Industry | Custom Furniture |
| Product | Customizable Gaming Tables |
| Deal Status | Deal secured with Robert |
| Investment Asked | $100,000 for 5% equity |
| Deal Outcome | $300,000 for 25% equity |
| Valuation | $2 million (at the time of the Shark Tank pitch) |

Gifford claimed he liked finding solutions for his problems and selling them. He made his Geek Chic furniture in Everett, Washington, for discerning gamers and geeks who wanted functionality paired with aesthetically pleasing furniture. [...] Gifford demonstrated one of his tables that doubles as a dining room table, showing how it opens up space for setting up games.

As impressed as the Sharks are with the quality and presentation of his furniture, the numbers have them nodding at first. Sales in the first year were $2 million, but the bottom line was less healthy.

The company was in the red for $100,000, and Gifford intended to use the investment to improve his manufacturing and shipping capabilities.

## Did Geek Chic Get a Deal on Shark Tank?

Lori Greiner loved Geek Chic but didn’t believe he could compete in the tough furniture industry, so she was out. Mark Cuban said, “Furniture? It’s just not me.” He only saw a table and didn’t want to be in that industry, so he was out. [...] Robert Herjavec liked the furniture but didn’t believe in the business model, so he was out.

Kevin O’Leary told Gifford he was “an anomaly” for getting this far in the furniture business. He thought Gifford should keep the company small instead of trying to scale it up, so he was out too.

Daymond John wasn’t sure he could “ride” with the “geek thing,” but he loved the furniture and how Gifford ran the company. He made an offer of $200,000 for 25%.

Gifford countered with $500,000 for 15%.

Daymond John wasn’t impressed and stood firm on his offer. Unexpectedly, Robert Herjavec jumped back in with a higher offer, putting up $300,000 for 25%. Gifford accepted Robert’s offer and left the Tank with a Shark deal.
